PLAN "12-Week Strength Programme for Dysmenorrhea-Aware Training"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Build full-body strength with cycle-aware modifications"
  GOAL secondary aerobic:
    name "Build aerobic base with cycle-aware cardio"
  GOAL tertiary conditioning:
    name "Improve metabolic conditioning with HIIT"
  GOAL quaternary power:
    name "Develop athletic power and plyometric ability"

PHASES
  PHASE "Cycle 1" (4 weeks):
    SUMMARY:
      - Weeks 1 and 4: Flow days (Mon/Wed) are low intensity, no HIIT, no plyometrics, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. Strength is moderate, RPE 6. Cardio is low intensity (walking, cycling, elliptical). 
      - Weeks 2 and 3: Post-flow, intensity increases to RPE 7. Strength sessions focus on full-body and upper/lower splits. Cardio is moderate, aerobic base. HIIT is low impact (rowing, battle_ropes, mountain_climber). No plyometrics yet.
      - Each week: 3 strength, 3 cardio, 1 HIIT. No plyometric/power day in this phase.
  PHASE "Cycle 2" (4 weeks):
    SUMMARY:
      - Week 5: Flow days (Mon/Wed) remain low intensity. From Friday, intensity increases: strength sessions at RPE 8, higher volume, longer rest. Plyometric/power day (Saturday) introduced post-flow (box_jump, jump_squat, push_up, medicine_ball_slam). HIIT day (Sunday) is high intensity.
      - Weeks 6-7: Strength and power sessions at high intensity (RPE 8), higher sets/reps, longer rest. Plyometric/power and HIIT days continue. Cardio remains moderate.
      - Week 8: Deload week, all sessions drop to RPE 6-7, lower volume, no HIIT or plyometrics.
      - Each week: 3-4 strength, 2-3 cardio, 1 plyometric/power, 1 HIIT.
  PHASE "Cycle 3" (4 weeks):
    SUMMARY:
      - Weeks 9 and 12: Flow days (Mon/Wed) are low intensity, no HIIT, no plyometrics, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. Strength is moderate, RPE 6. Cardio is low intensity. 
      - Weeks 10-11: Post-flow, intensity returns to RPE 7. Strength, plyometric/power, and HIIT days continue. Cardio remains moderate.
      - Week 12: Deload for most of the week. Friday is a 1RM testing day for squat, bench_press, and deadlift (6x1, RPE 9, long rest). No HIIT or plyometrics on flow days.
      - Each week: 3 strength, 2-3 cardio, 1 plyometric/power, 1 HIIT. Week 12 includes 1RM testing.

NUTRITION
  STRATEGY "Cycle-Supportive Nutrition":
    GENERAL:
      - Eat a balanced diet with lean protein, complex carbohydrates, healthy fats, and plenty of vegetables and fruits.
      - Hydrate: Aim for at least 2.5L water daily, increase during flow days.
      - Limit processed foods, excess sugar, and caffeine, especially during flow days.
    FLOW DAYS (Days 1-3 of cycle):
      - Increase magnesium-rich foods (spinach, pumpkin seeds, almonds, black beans) to help reduce cramping.
      - Prioritize iron-rich foods (lean red meat, lentils, spinach, tofu) to support blood loss.
      - Include vitamin C sources (citrus, bell peppers, broccoli) to aid iron absorption.
      - Add omega-3 sources (salmon, chia seeds, walnuts, flaxseed) to help reduce inflammation.
      - Eat smaller, more frequent meals if appetite is low or nausea is present.
      - Avoid salty foods to minimize bloating.
      - Herbal teas (ginger, chamomile, peppermint) may help with cramps and nausea.
    POST-FLOW (Days 4-14):
      - Maintain balanced meals with emphasis on protein and complex carbs to support recovery and energy.
      - Continue hydration and include colorful vegetables for micronutrients.
    LUTEAL PHASE (Days 15-28):
      - Increase complex carbohydrates (quinoa, oats, sweet potato, brown rice) to support energy and mood.
      - Include foods rich in B vitamins (whole grains, eggs, legumes) for energy and PMS support.
      - Continue magnesium and omega-3 intake.
      - Monitor cravings and opt for healthy snacks (fruit, yogurt, nuts).
      - Maintain hydration and fiber intake to reduce bloating.
    SUPPLEMENTS (if cleared by GP):
      - Consider magnesium glycinate (200-400mg), vitamin B6, and fish oil for cramp and PMS support.
      - Iron supplement if blood tests indicate deficiency.
